items.title: Inside fast-growing consumer brand Clean Cult’s carton crusade
items.summary: Paper-based cartons and other fiber packaging alternatives to plastic continue to expand in the food and beverage sector, with sales nearing $500 billion in 2026.

items.title: No more ‘who shouts the loudest’: How Aldi decided where to spend on sustainability
items.summary: Supermarket chain Aldi Süd is known as a sustainability leader, in part through its decision to hold tight to its emissions reduction targets even as it pursues ambitious growth plans in the U.S. and U.K. What’s less clear is whether it can meet those climate goals.

items.title: Why automated product carbon footprints aren’t yet ‘decision-grade’
items.summary: Just a few years ago, creating a product carbon footprint (PCF) — an estimate of net greenhouse gas emissions over the product’s lifecycle — was an arduous process requiring weeks or months spent searching for relevant data.

items.title: EV target cuts could increase UK petrol dependence by 130 million barrels
items.summary: # EV target cuts could increase UK petrol dependence by 130 million barrels New research has found that proposed Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Mandate changes could increase UK oil and petrol import dependence by almost 130 million barrels by 2050.

items.title: Plans to shake up Natural England and Environment Agency spark green backlash
items.summary: # Plans to shake up Natural England and Environment Agency spark green backlash The First Secretary of State has confirmed arms-length Government bodies like Natural England are under review, drawing criticism from green groups.

items.title: How decarbonising business travel can be a lever for wider sustainability
items.summary: # How decarbonising business travel can be a lever for wider sustainability Addressing business travel can help embed a sustainability mindset across an organisation, even when travel is not its largest emissions source.

items.title: Only a quarter of businesses understand the EU’s new packaging regulations
items.summary: # Only a quarter of businesses understand the EU’s new packaging regulations A new survey has found that around a quarter of businesses feel they understand new European packaging and waste regulations.

items.title: More than 800 UK businesses could face review of renewable electricity tariffs under new rules
items.summary: # More than 800 UK businesses could face review of renewable electricity tariffs under new rules New research has found that 842 UK-headquartered organisations could be affected by new corporate climate reporting requirements that will place greater scrutiny on claims of using 100% renewable electricity.
